name: Karaoke caption sync
looks: Over real talking-head footage, a line of captions sits low in the frame. As the speaker says each word, that word gets a highlight box or colour fill exactly on the syllable, while words before it stay base-coloured and words after are not yet visible. The highlight travels word to word in lockstep with the audio.
build: One DOM line of word spans with per-word start/end times. renderCaptions(t) sets each word's class (past/active/future) from the master clock; the active word's highlight scales in (0.9->1, 0.08s) exactly at its start time, with no easing on the switch itself.
sound: The real or simulated speech audio is the timing source; a very light tick on each word can reinforce it in a silent preview.
prompt: Over real talking-head footage, caption the speech with a word-by-word highlight that lands exactly on each word as it is said, the spoken words staying lit and the rest base-coloured, so the caption reads as live transcription, not a static subtitle.
source: a Matra captions-app promo in prompt-motion.com's gallery (prompt-motion.com/gautam-mer1-2ae354), studied 2026-10-09
